papers.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sequence Models for Sample-Efficient Energy Regression in Simulated Calorimeter Showers
papers.abstract: Energy reconstruction from electromagnetic calorimeter data underpins particle identification, event reconstruction and precision measurements in high-energy physics. Machine learning already performs well on this task, yet two questions remain open: how much the choice of data representation matters, and whether hybrid quantum-classical models add value in practice. We compare classical and quantum-enhanced models for incident positron energy reconstruction on the CaloGAN dataset, a public benchmark of 100,000 simulated electromagnetic shower events spanning 1 to 100 GeV. Eight architectures, namely SVR, ANN, CNN and LSTM together with their quantum counterparts, are trained on three calorimeter representations: engineered physical features, calorimeter images, and longitudinal shower sequences. Models that follow the longitudinal development of the shower reach the highest accuracy, which points to the value of physically informed representations. The hybrid QLSTM gives the lowest reconstruction error, with an RMSE of 0.294 GeV. Under matched-data conditions with only 1,500 training events, the QLSTM improves on the classical LSTM by 52.7% and also surpasses an LSTM trained on the full set. These observations indicate that longitudinal representations are central to calorimeter energy reconstruction and give preliminary evidence that hybrid quantum-classical sequence models can be more sample-efficient for regression in high-energy physics.

papers.title: The Full-Shape Analysis of the Fading Dark Sector Model
papers.abstract: We analyze the Fading Dark Sector (FDS) model, which is motivated by string theory and in which the fading of the dark sector is driven by a scalar field. The model is specified by two $O(1)$ numbers $(c,c')$ that parametrize the logarithmic derivatives of the dark energy and dark matter densities with respect to the field in Planck units. In previous work, we showed that this model provides a good fit to the DESI BAO, CMB, and SN datasets. Here, we extend that analysis to include the DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy power spectrum, which adds information about the time evolution of cosmic structure and provides an independent consistency check of the FDS model. We find that, when the DESI DR1 full-shape data are combined with CMB+DESI DR2 BAO+DES-Dovekie, the FDS model outperforms the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization by $\Delta \chi^2_{\rm MAP}=-4$ at equal parameter count and is preferred over $\Lambda$CDM at $4.1\sigma$. The inferred values of $(c,c')$ with the full-shape data are unchanged from our previous analysis, so this improvement indicates that FDS makes a prediction for the growth of structure that captures the observed growth history better than the $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization.

papers.title: Microscopic Realizability of Non-unique Bubble Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions drive fluid motion that induces energy transport and gravitational-wave production. The flows are usually classified in terms of the wall velocity and the transition strength. We show that this description fails when the two phases have unequal sound speeds $c_\pm$. New mixed-hybrid profiles may appear, and for a strong hierarchy, $c_+\gg c_-$, where the phase behind the wall is much softer, heating or cooling ahead of the wall allow for the coexistence of distinct stationary flows at the same wall velocity and transition strength. This ambiguity is removed once thermodynamic normalization and entropy production are specified. We identify microscopic settings that realize these sound-speed hierarchies. In thermal plasmas it requires exponentially large mass-to-temperature ratios, whereas at finite density a conserved charge removes this obstruction, making dense matter its natural arena.

papers.title: Hydr\'oDex: gotta match 'em all!
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive hydrodynamic classification of stationary fluid profiles in first-order phase transitions within the constant-sound-speed model, a physically motivated extension of the standard bag model that allows the sound speeds in front of and behind the wall, $c_+$ and $c_-$, to differ. Solving the matching conditions at the bubble wall and evolving the profile in the surrounding plasma, we systematically identify and classify all the possible stationary solutions. The classification recovers all previously known direct and inverse detonation, deflagration, and hybrid solutions, while revealing a new class of stationary configurations, termed mixed hybrids, featuring rarefaction waves on both sides of the wall and oppositely directed fluid flows. For a sufficiently pronounced hierarchy $c_+ > c_-$, the classification in terms of the wall velocity $\xi_w$ and the asymptotic strength parameter $\alpha_N$ further exhibits degenerate regions in parameter space, where multiple distinct stationary profiles correspond to the same physical inputs $(\xi_w,\alpha_N)$. This non-uniqueness arises as the parametrization discards thermodynamic information and is resolved once the underlying microphysics is specified. We also compute the kinetic-energy budget and the associated acoustic gravitational-wave spectra within the sound-shell model, finding that mixed-hybrid solutions, despite their oppositely directed flows, introduce no additional spectral feature, and their spectra can be closely mimicked by ordinary direct or inverse hybrids with very different fluid profiles. Finally, we release Hydr\'oDex, a public code that implements the complete hydrodynamic classification, fluid-profile construction, kinetic-energy budget, and gravitational-wave calculation.

papers.title: Many-body Response to Spin-Independent and Spin-Dependent Dark Matter Scattering in a Superfluid Helium-3 Target
papers.abstract: The QUEST-DMC experiment employs an ultra-low-temperature superfluid $^3$He target in an effort to detect sub-GeV dark matter (DM). The low-momentum scattering of such light DM is sensitive to the many-body structure of superfluid $^3$He, making it necessary to account for the collective behaviour of the medium. We present a first-principles calculation of the DM scattering rate in this inherently quantum many-body medium for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions. The leading consequence of this many-body behaviour is a kinematic enhancement of the scattering rate arising from the Fermi-Dirac statistics of the ultra-low-temperature target. Accounting for this extends the projected reach to lower DM masses for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions under the benchmark detector assumptions considered here. The resulting sensitivity improvement becomes increasingly pronounced as the detector threshold drops into the sub-eV regime. It is negligible at the conventional readout threshold of approximately $31$ eV, but becomes significant at the $0.51$ eV benchmark threshold for SQUID-based readout. Specifically, at this threshold, incorporating the many-body response extends the higher-energy recoil tail and improves the projected low-mass reach by approximately $2.5\%$ relative to the single-atom approximation. This improvement becomes more pronounced at lower thresholds. Reaching a threshold of $5$ meV could further extend the sensitivity of QUEST-DMC into the realm of sub-MeV DM.

papers.title: Gravitational production of dark QED by the trace anomaly
papers.abstract: We revisit the production of fermionic dark matter $\chi$ through the graviton portal, sourced by inflaton annihilation at the end of inflation. Because the production rate is helicity-suppressed, $\propto m_\chi^2$, the dark fermion must be very heavy to account for the observed relic abundance, $m_\chi \gtrsim 10^{10}$ GeV, with the exact bound set by the reheating temperature $T_{\rm RH}$. Here we examine how interactions within the dark sector could modify this result. As a toy model, we consider dark QED, in which $\chi$ couples to a light dark photon. We first show that, as a consequence of classical conformal invariance, bremsstrahlung of a dark photon does not lift the helicity suppression for light fermions. We then show that the trace anomaly of dark QED, which affects the coupling of the graviton to dark photons, can produce light dark fermions via a Dalitz process. This allows to extend the fermionic dark mass range possibly down to $m_\chi \sim 10^7$~GeV, depending on $T_{\rm RH}$ and the dark QED coupling. We also determine under which conditions the hidden sector reaches thermal equilibrium and derive a lower bound on the temperature ratio at reheating $(T'/T)_{\rm RH}$ as function of the dark QED coupling and the reheating temperature.

papers.title: The Sound of Dark Sectors in Pulsar Timing Arrays
papers.abstract: A phase transition in the dark sector (DS) presents a promising explanation for the stochastic gravitational wave (GW) signals detected in recent observations by Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs). Instead of focusing solely on fitting data with phenomenological parameters, we systematically delineate simple, underlying DS models at the microscopic, Lagrangian level and uncover the conditions required to yield the GW spectrum observed by PTAs. Within this framework, the characteristic scale of the dark sector is $O$(MeV), with complementary tests at future energy- and intensity-frontier experiments.

papers.title: Quasicrystalline Inflation: From the Cosmological Dipole to Primordial Diffraction
papers.abstract: We propose quasicrystalline inflation. Six quasiperiodic phases decompose into three phonons and three phasons. It turns out that a coherent pure-phason displacement can generate a local power dipole while the linear traceless quadrupole vanishes. From spatially varying quadratic effective field theory, we derive off-diagonal correlations whose momentum transfer is restricted to integer combinations of the six icosahedral wavevectors. These correlated off-diagonal signals provide a characteristic observational signature of primordial quasiperiodic order, primordial diffraction.

papers.title: Rank-One Ultralight Dark Matter Response in a Full-Tensor Gravity Gradiometer
papers.abstract: A full-tensor superconducting gravity gradiometer whose four test masses carry two compositions in a $2+2$ pattern acquires a composition-dependent channel for dilaton-coupled ultralight dark matter. The reconstructed response is the rank-one tensor $\K=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, with the axis of $\qv$ fixed in advance by the material assignment, and obeys the parameter-free null condition $\K(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$, which no gravity gradient or platform rotation alone can satisfy; it vanishes for a single composition. For copper and lead, the sensitivity reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$, and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers.

papers.title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
papers.abstract: Supernova cooling provides some of the strongest constraints on light particles beyond the Standard Model, including sub-GeV dark matter (DM). While sufficiently large couplings to the Standard Model sector can trap these particles inside the supernova or cause them to decay before escaping, there typically exists an intermediate range of couplings in which their efficient production and subsequent escape lead to excessive energy loss, resulting in stringent constraints on new light particles. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that, for certain types of DM-neutrino interactions, resonantly enhanced $s$-channel scattering with neutrinos can efficiently trap DM inside the supernova and can fundamentally alter the conventional supernova cooling constraints. In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature, this resonant scattering can prevent a substantial fraction of the produced DM from freely escaping, thereby significantly weakening, or even evading, the usual supernova cooling constraints on such models.

papers.title: Improved Bounds on the Dark Matter-Neutrino Cross Section using LSBGs
Suprathermal bulk viscosity in binary neutron star mergers
papers.abstract: Numerical relativity simulations of binary neutron star mergers and core-collapse supernovae indicate that the neutron star matter can be driven far from equilibrium due to large amplitude density oscillations, with frequency in the kHz range. Urca processes in neutron star matter try to restore the system towards equilibrium providing strong bulk viscous damping of these density oscillations. Standard bulk viscosity calculations typically assume small amplitude density oscillations, such that the deviation from chemical equilibrium $\mu_{\Delta}$ is less than the temperature $T$. In this work we compute the complete amplitude dependent bulk viscosity, taking into account, for the first time, thermal blurring effects and collisional broadening of in-medium nucleons. Our results show that the non-linear effects in bulk viscosity start to become important when the oscillation amplitude is about $10$ percent of the background density. In this regime the bulk viscosity can increase by three to five orders of magnitude. These results have important consequences for simulations of binary neutron star mergers as well as their multi-messenger observations.

papers.title: Constraints on ultralight bosons from merging binary and remnant black holes observed during the second and third parts of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
authors: J. F. J. van den Brand
papers.abstract: We present constraints on ultralight bosons using binary black hole mergers observed in the second and third parts of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run. Directed searches are conducted for long-transient gravitational waves from ultralight vector boson clouds around merger remnants, using a hidden-Markov-model (HMM) tracking scheme. We target the remnant black holes formed in the binary coalescences that produced GW250114 and GW250207. We find no evidence for such signals from either target. Estimating our search sensitivity at a threshold corresponding to a 1% false alarm probability, we thus disfavor vector boson masses in the range of $[2.80, 3.95]\times 10^{-13}$ eV with greater than 90% confidence. In addition, we derive constraints on ultralight scalar and vector bosons from the inferred high spins of the constituent black holes in three binaries, using events GW240515, GW241113, and GW241225_08. The excluded mass ranges in this approach depend on the assumed black-hole ages. At $10^5$ years, corresponding to typical dynamically formed binaries, we exclude scalar and vector bosons in the ranges $[1.39, 6.94]\times 10^{-13}$ eV and $[0.32, 14.4]\times 10^{-13}$ eV at 90% confidence, respectively.

papers.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
papers.abstract: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform-mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW. Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2\sigma$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.

papers.title: Baryon and lepton asymmetries across the cosmic QCD transition: effects of a 3D first-order surface
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological QCD phase transition by calculating the cosmic trajectories from the five equations that impose the conservation of the baryon and lepton asymmetries, the charge neutrality of the Universe, and $\beta$ equilibrium. We perform the calculation using for the first time the four-dimensional $(T, \mu_B, \mu_Q, \mu_S)$ Constant Entropy Contour equation of state, which for $\mu_S = 0$ ($\beta$-equilibrium) features a critical line and a first-order phase transition (FOPT) surface in the three-dimensional $(T, \mu_B, \mu_Q)$ space. We first show that, within the standard cosmological scenario with baryon asymmetry $b_{\text{obs}}=8.65\cdot 10^{-11}$, the lepton asymmetries alone can never induce a FOPT. We then explore the non-standard cosmological scenario with large values of $b$ and find that reaching a FOPT requires $b\gtrsim0.028$ during the QCD epoch. Such a value is compatible with observations only if the baryon asymmetry is diluted to $b_{\text{obs}}$ after the transition, which a period of little inflation would provide with $N\approx6.5$ $e$-folds of expansion. Finally, we study the phenomenological imprints on the equation of state and primordial black hole (PBH) formation, showing that pion condensation at large lepton asymmetries drives $c_s^2 > 1/3$ and shifts the PBH peak to sub-solar masses ($0.3-0.8\,M_\odot$), while the large-$b$ FOPT yields a narrow spike around $4.2\,M_\odot$.

papers.title: Unitarity bounds and sum rules in the SMEFT: a systematic analysis
papers.abstract: We present a systematic analysis of perturbative unitarity bounds and spinning sum rules in the baryon-number-conserving dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), with particular emphasis on flavor structure. Employing an on-shell partial-wave formalism for generic $N \to M$ scattering amplitudes, we perform a coupled-channel analysis of the complete operator basis and derive bounds on individual Wilson coefficients by marginalizing over the remaining interactions. We formulate spinning sum rules for four-fermion operators in the Warsaw basis and translate their flavor-space definiteness conditions into constraints on Wilson coefficients, under specified assumptions about the ultraviolet dynamics. We then extend both analyses to the three-generation four-fermion sector within Minimal Flavor Violation, retaining leading up-type Yukawa insertions, and an exact $U(2)^5$ flavor symmetry. The resulting constraints reveal correlations among flavor structures that are absent in the single-flavor limit. Through explicit matching to representative ultraviolet completions, we illustrate how spinning sum rules can distinguish scalar- from vector-mediated interactions, while also identifying the limitations of this interpretation. These results provide a general framework for assessing the consistency of new-physics scenarios within the SMEFT, relying on minimal theoretical assumptions.

papers.title: Positivity Bounds, Negative Running, and the Weak Gravity Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study causality and unitarity constraints at one loop on a low-energy effective theory containing a photon, a massless scalar coupled to it through dilaton-like interactions, and a light neutral Dirac fermion with a Yukawa coupling to the scalar. In this setup, non-gravitational loop effects induced by the Yukawa interaction can drive the coefficient of the four-photon $(F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu})^2$ operator negative at low energies, apparently violating the tree-level positivity bound. Nevertheless, we find that these negative values are consistent with one-loop constraints from causality and unitarity, thanks to the low-energy contribution from the massless scalar to the relevant dispersion relation. We also examine the implications of this negative running for the Weak Gravity Conjecture in the magnetic limit of Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes, since the RG-evolved Wilson coefficients can a priori shift the extremality condition towards the subextremal region. We find, however, that this shift is obstructed by the fermion mass induced by the same Yukawa coupling, which prevents the fermion from contributing to the running of the relevant operators down to the low-energy scales required to make the black holes subextremal. Finally, we discuss the relevance of negative running to loop-level positivity bounds in the SMEFT and to light-by-light scattering in the presence of a light scalar.

papers.title: What Comes Out Of Monopole-Fermion Scattering?
papers.abstract: We describe what happens when chiral fermions scatter off magnetic monopoles. It has long been known that, in many situations, the outgoing state cannot be constructed from any finite number of excitations. In the language of 2d CFT, it lives in a twisted sector of the Hilbert space. Here we explain what this means from the perspective of a d=3+1 observer. We show that an ingoing one-particle excitation is scattered into an outgoing state surrounded by a soft cloud which consists of an infinite number of low energy particle-anti-particle pairs. We compute energy and charge correlators, showing that this cloud fragments in any measurement. A detector will register one or more hard particles which leave tracks and carry standard quantum numbers. The remaining exotic quantum numbers live in the soft cloud, and are characterised by large charge fluctuations in the detector

papers.title: Subleading beauty effects in Higgs production at small transverse momentum
papers.abstract: We study $b$-quark mass effects at small Higgs transverse momentum $q_T$ where the Higgs is produced in gluon fusion via a closed $b$-quark loop. In contrast to top-quark loops, which can be integrated out at a high scale, the $b$-quark mass, $m_b$, induces a second small scale $m_b \sim q_T \ll m_H$ such that standard $q_T$ resummation does not apply in this region, which includes the peak of the distribution. The resummation of mass effects for the $gg\to H$ form factor, which has been studied previously, applies to the $q_T$ spectrum in the limit $q_T \ll m_b$. Unlike this case, for $q_T \sim m_b$, real emissions can resolve the $b$-quark loop, requiring a more complicated simultaneous $m_b$ and $q_T$ factorization. It involves new next-to-leading-power $m_b$ and $q_T$ dependent beam and soft functions, and the corresponding bare factorization theorem suffers - as expected - from endpoint divergences. We use soft-collinear effective theory to explicitly compute all amplitudes with a $b$-quark loop and an additional real soft or collinear emission. Our results provide important insight into the nontrivial structure of the endpoint divergences and show how their expected cancellation happens in the sum of all amplitudes separately for soft and collinear emissions. Interestingly, we find that at this order the endpoint-divergent contributions have a separable dependence on $q_T$ and $m_b$, providing strong motivation that in the future their cancellations can be made manifest in the factorized cross section. As an important further cross check we show that the sum of all SCET amplitudes correctly reproduces the full-QCD one-emission amplitudes expanded in the relevant soft or collinear limit, which also requires nontrivial contributions involving massive Glauber quarks in the effective-theory calculation.

papers.title: Geometric Bounds on Axion-Photon Couplings in Non-Supersymmetric Heterotic Compactifications
papers.abstract: We study the photon couplings of QCD axions and axion-like particles in non-supersymmetric heterotic string theory on Calabi-Yau threefolds with line bundles. After the St\"uckelberg mechanism and anomaly matching are taken into account, the QCD axion direction is determined by the QCD axion-coupling coefficients together with the axion kinetic matrix. We focus on the electromagnetic-to-color axion coupling ratio, $E/N$. When the physical electromagnetic and QCD axion-coupling vectors are proportional with the ratio fixed by the gauge levels, the QCD axion has $E/N=8/3$ for $k_3=k_2=1$ and $k_Y=5/3$, independently of the axion kinetic matrix. It is found that direct flux breaking of the visible $SO(16)_{\rm v}$ can produce independent QCD and electromagnetic axion-coupling vectors for the same level assignment. The Hermitian Yang-Mills equations and the heterotic Bianchi identity then restrict the departure from $8/3$. We derive analytic bounds for backgrounds with and without five-brane charge under assumptions about the axion kinetic terms and low-energy matching. An $SU(5)$-like model and a direct-flux Standard-Model-like model illustrate proportional and independent Green-Schwarz coupling vectors, respectively. For axions with no QCD coupling, we derive a geometric upper bound on their photon couplings and evaluate it in an explicit compactification.

papers.title: Searching for signatures of criticality in heavy-ion collisions using two-pion correlation functions
papers.abstract: We study possible signatures of the existence of a Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) critical end-point in low-energy relativistic heavy-ion collisions using two-pion femtoscopy. We simulate central $^{209}\mathrm{Bi}+^{209}\mathrm{Bi}$ collisions at center-of-mass energies ranging from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.8$ to 11 GeV using the EPOS 4.0.3 framework, incorporating an equation of state that explicitly includes a critical end-point and is compatible with lattice QCD results at small baryon chemical potentials. We analyze the pion pair-distance distribution and the corresponding two-pion correlation function by fitting them with L\'evy distributions in configuration and momentum spaces, respectively. We find a weak dependence of the source parameters on the collision energy below $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=9.2$ GeV, followed by a change in trend at higher energies, particularly in the intercept parameter $\lambda$. This behavior may be associated with a decreasing fraction of pions coming from the core and an increasing contribution from long-lived resonance decays. Within the present analysis, we do not identify an unambiguous signal attributable to the critical end-point. A comparison with simulations employing different equation of state parameters to vary the strength of the critical point, as well as with simulations without a critical end-point, is necessary to establish the sensitivity of these observables to critical phenomena.

papers.title: Spin asymmetry in vacuum pair production under polarized electric fields
papers.abstract: We study spin-resolved electron--positron pair production from the quantum vacuum in spatially homogeneous, time-dependent electric fields with linear, elliptical, and circular polarizations. The equal-time Dirac--Heisenberg--Wigner formalism is employed to compute the final momentum distributions in two distinct frequency regimes, for both unchirped and chirped field configurations. In the high-frequency regime, characterized by a reference Keldysh parameter, linearly polarized fields yield identical particle yields for the two spin projections considered, whereas elliptical and circular polarizations generate pronounced spin-resolved population imbalances near the dominant multiphoton resonance. Frequency chirping broadens the resonant spectral structures and extends the momentum range over which a sizable normalized spin difference persists. In the low-frequency regime, the pair-production spectra are governed by quantum tunneling and temporal interference effects. Although the peak spin asymmetry in this regime is substantially weaker than in the high-frequency case, the normalized differential spectra still exhibit sign-changing interference fringes. We find that the spin-asymmetry degree exceeds 90$\%$ for circular polarization in the high-frequency regime, while it saturates at approximately 20$\%$ in the low-frequency regime. Given the purely electric background field, we interpret these results in terms of spin-projected Wigner components and the handed time dependence of rotating electric fields, while clearly distinguishing normalized spectral differences from local or integrated polarization observables.

papers.title: Emerging understanding of the rare kaon decay $K^+\to\pi^+\ell^+\ell^-$ from lattice QCD
papers.abstract: Rare kaon decays provide sensitive probes of the Standard Model and potential new physics. For $K^+\to\pi^+\ell^+\ell^-$, the experimental decay rate determines only the squared vector form factor $|V(z)|^2$, leaving its sign undetermined. Previous lattice QCD calculations have either used unphysical pion masses or suffered from uncertainties too large to resolve this sign. Here we present a first-principles calculation using two domain-wall fermion ensembles with near-physical pion masses. We develop a computational strategy that establishes the ultraviolet finiteness and continuum equivalence of local and conserved vector currents, substantially simplifying the calculation of nonlocal matrix elements. Four independent subtraction schemes provide nontrivial consistency checks, while the one-end trick reduces noise from quark-self-loop contributions. We determine $V(z)$ at six spacelike and timelike momentum transfers. Fits consistently yield $V(0)<0$, with a statistical significance of $5.8\sigma$--$7.9\sigma$ at $M_{\eta_c}=1.1,\mathrm{GeV}$. After extrapolation to the physical charm-quark mass, the negative sign persists across all fit forms, with a significance of $2.0\sigma$--$3.4\sigma$. Our results provide direct first-principles evidence favoring the negative-sign solution and establish a framework for more precise lattice QCD determinations.

papers.title: LHC Based Antimuon-Nucleus Collider LH$\mu$C: Nucleus Options
papers.abstract: Nucleus options of the LH$\mu$C, an antimuon-hadron collider based on the LHC, are presented. Ultra-cold $\mu^+$ beams, based on the technology of the J-PARC muon $g-2$/EDM experiment as proposed for $\mu$TRISTAN, are accelerated to 1 TeV in either a $\mu$TRISTAN-type booster or a booster housed in the LH$e$C energy-recovery-linac tunnel, and collide with LHC nucleus beams in a 3 km main ring tangential to the LHC. Collisions with Pb, Xe, O and Ne beams provide centre-of-mass energies from 13.1 to 47.9 TeV, i.e. about 3.3 TeV per nucleon. Luminosities and beam-beam tune shifts are evaluated with the AloHEP software. For $\mu$-Pb collisions, the luminosity reaches $2.7\times10^{30}$ ($2.2\times10^{30}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ with the $\mu$TRISTAN-type (ERL-based) booster, i.e. $5.6\times10^{32}$ ($4.5\times10^{32}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ per nucleon, which a Brinkmann-Dohlus dynamic focusing scheme could increase by a factor of 2-3. The physics potential is discussed, including an extension of the kinematic reach by a factor of about 20 with respect to the LH$e$C, access to parton saturation at perturbative scales, nuclear parton distributions, photon-induced processes and charged-current flavour separation.

papers.title: Holographic Butterfly Velocity and Heavy-Quark Drag in a Doubly Anisotropic Magnetized QGP
papers.abstract: We investigate butterfly velocity and heavy-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma with two distinct sources of anisotropy, generated by collision geometry and an external magnetic field, within a five-dimensional holographic model exhibiting magnetic catalysis. In contrast to studies restricted to isotropic or singly anisotropic media, we analyze the butterfly velocity and heavy-quark drag force along all three orthogonal spatial directions at finite temperature and chemical potential in the deconfined phase. We find that the collision-induced anisotropy plays a dominant role in the directional dependence of both butterfly velocity and heavy-quark drag. It governs the directional splitting of the butterfly velocity, and significantly enhances the parallel drag force while suppressing the transverse components. For butterfly velocity, a strong magnetic field primarily suppresses the longitudinal butterfly velocity while leaving the transverse components nearly unchanged. For the drag force, the magnetic field breaks the transverse symmetry, yet it does not alter the overall monotonic increase of the drag force with heavy-quark velocity, temperature, and chemical potential. Most importantly, by bridging the Einstein and string frames via the Weyl transformation, we extract the frame-dependent drag-chaos relation. Generalizing it to the doubly anisotropic plasma, we demonstrate that despite the underlying frame-dependent chaos, the normalized directional drag exhibits a direction-dependent geometric correction at order $\mathcal{O}(v^{3})$. These results establish a direction-resolved connection between heavy-quark dissipation, information scrambling, and the underlying anisotropic geometry of magnetized QGP.

papers.title: $B \to D$ form factors from light-cone sum rules
papers.abstract: We present a light-cone sum rule (LCSR) analysis of the $B\to D$ transition form factors $f_+^{BD}(q^2)$ and $f_0^{BD}(q^2)$ in the large-recoil region, including the next-to-leading-power corrections at tree level. The non-perturbative input is provided by the leading-twist $D$-meson distribution amplitude determined from lattice QCD in the heavy-quark large-momentum effective theory (HQLaMET) framework, which enters together with the twist-three and twist-four distribution amplitudes of the $D$ meson fixed by the QCD equations of motion. A combined fit to the LCSR results at $q^2\lesssim2$~GeV$^2$ and to the FNAL/MILC and HPQCD lattice data at $q^2\gtrsim8.5$~GeV$^2$, performed in the model-independent Boyd-Grinstein-Lebed (BGL) parametrisation, allows us to obtain the form factors over the whole physical range and to extract $|V_{cb}|$ from the semileptonic $B\to D\ell\nu$ decay as well as the lepton-flavour universality ratio $R(D)$.

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of $\rho$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD
papers.abstract: We compute the gravitational form factors and mechanical properties of the $\rho$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD, a holographic model of QCD with backreacting flavor and dynamical chiral symmetry breaking. The parameters of the model are taken from an earlier fit to meson spectra and are not adjusted to form factor data. Both mesons are described by a single spin-1 field, and the six form factors are identified from the matrix element of the energy-momentum tensor with two spin-1 states, following the holographic dictionary. We find that $A_0 = J$ and $A_1 = 0$ hold identically in the model, and show that the remaining form factors $E$, $D_0$ and $D_1$ are regular at zero momentum transfer. We compare the form factors of $\rho$ with results from the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, a light-cone constituent quark model and the hard-wall holographic model. From the form factors, we compute the monopole and quadrupole distributions of energy, pressure and shear force in the Breit frame. The D-term, defined for spin-1 hadrons as the forward value of the combination $\mathcal{D}_0(t)$ of form factors, is found to be $-2.98$ for the $\rho$ and $-7.43$ for the $a_1$ meson. The mass and mechanical radii are $0.81$~fm and $0.89$~fm for $\rho$, and $0.73$~fm and $0.80$~fm for $a_1$.

papers.title: ESME stays positive: event generation with positive weights
papers.abstract: Fully differential simulations of hard-scattering processes are a cornerstone of precision phenomenology at collider experiments. For long, Monte Carlo event generators have been able to achieve next-to-leading order (NLO) accuracy, but their results typically suffer from the presence of negative-weight events. These degrade statistical power and complicate downstream analyses. In this contribution, we present Exponentiated Subtraction for Matching Events (ESME), a novel approach to NLO+PS matching that yields positive-definite event weights while preserving perturbative accuracy and the logarithmic structure of the shower. We discuss the formalism and its implementation within the PanScales framework.

papers.title: Metastable vortex string decay in a brane picture
papers.abstract: We describe the decay of a metastable string as a bounce in a brane configuration. We consider a particular $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric $\mathrm{U}(2)$ gauge theory with cascade Higgsing $\mathrm{U}(2)\to \mathrm{U}(1)^2 \to \mathrm{U}(1)$, where the vortex string can break by creating a pair of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole and anti-monopole. The theory is engineered in a Type IIA brane setup, where the metastable string is realized as a D2-brane stretched between NS5- and D4-branes. The string breaks when the endpoints of the D2-brane, moving along the NS5- and D4-branes, meet so that the D2-brane shrinks to nothing. We check that the tension of the D2-brane reproduces that of the vortex string obtained numerically in the field theory, with the ratio approaching one in the limit where the vortex string becomes BPS. Within the thin-wall approximation, we derive the bounce action from the Dirac-Born-Infeld action of the D2-brane and find that it agrees with that of the field theory, with the monopole mass given by the area swept by the D2-brane. As a consistency check, we numerically construct a bounce solution of the D2-brane equation of motion under simplifying assumptions, whose action agrees with the thin-wall result in the regime where our description is reliable.

papers.title: Probing Dirac Heavy Neutral Leptons through EFT-Induced Meson Decays
papers.abstract: We investigate dimension-six operators involving pairs of Dirac-type heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at beam-dump and far-forward experiments. In the $\nu$SMEFT framework, lepton-number-conserving four-fermion operators couple HNL pairs to quarks and induce two and three-body charm and bottom meson decays. We study the $c\to u$, $b\to d$, and $b\to s$ transitions at FASER2, FACET, SHiP, and two FPF@FCC configurations. HNL production depends on the cut-off scale $\Lambda$, while the lifetime depends on the active-sterile mixing $|V_{eN}|^2$. Sizable production can therefore coexist with the small mixing needed for HNLs to reach distant detectors. We project sensitivities in the $(M_N,|V_{eN}|^2)$ and $(M_N,\Lambda)$ planes, accounting for two and three-body decays and constraints from invisible and semivisible meson decays. SHiP is particularly sensitive to $c\to u$, while the larger FCC-LLP2 configuration probes $b\to d, s$. We find that EFT-induced pair production extends long-lived HNL searches to very small mixing and complements other probes of the $\nu$SMEFT heavy-neutrino sector.
